pages.title: Adopt cached renders for repeat exports
pages.verdict: Cache rendered pages. The sample shows the saving is real and no page failed; the open large-image case limits where the pilot runs, not whether caching works.
interpretations: Repeat exports of an unchanged ten-page deck take two thirds of the baseline time.
No page failed in either path across the 20 runs; caching did not cost reliability.

pages.title: Export time fell for eight weeks and sits just above target
pages.interpretation: Cached renders brought the fictional sample from 12.4 s to 8.2 s. The latest week is still 0.2 s above the 8 s ceiling, so the pilot stays with the platform team.
pages.measurementContext: Fictional pilot: mean of 20 scripted exports of the same ten-page deck each Monday; seconds per export.

pages.title: Where the cache sits in the export path

items.heading: Render once per page
items.body: Each page renders on the capture host exactly as before; caching changes nothing about how a page looks.

items.heading: Check the cache before capture
items.body: A page whose content and layout have not changed reuses the previous PNG instead of recapturing.

items.heading: Capture only what changed
items.body: Edited pages, hidden toggles, and failed loads always go through a fresh capture.
